nodes.label: Autodarts Board Manager local protocol (reverse-engineered)
nodes.rationale: Board Manager v1.0.7 at 192.168.120.40:3180; evidence lives in recon/captures/.

nodes.label: live-ws-2026-08-20 capture as replay fixture
nodes.rationale: Worth keeping because it is a real three-dart-then-takeout sequence, not a synthesised one.

nodes.label: Throw payload (state frame)
nodes.rationale: Each throw carries both coords and segment -- raw position and a resolved segment -- so we get heatmaps and grouping for free without owning segment mapping.

nodes.label: Board control (start/stop/reset/calibrate)
nodes.rationale: The buttons sit in the header because Reset and Calibrate are wanted mid-game with darts in hand and the board misreading. Each button is exactly one Board Manager endpoint and nothing more -- stopping detection does not end the match. Calls go frontend -> server -> bridge -> board because the bridge is the only process that knows a board's address and the board may be on a different network than the UI.

nodes.label: Local control API under /api
nodes.rationale: All unauthenticated because auth.api_key is empty in this board's config. PUT /api/start and /api/stop for detection, POST /api/reset for the throw counter, POST /api/config/calibration/auto for auto-calibration, GET /api/state for the snapshot, MJPEG streams under /api/streams.

nodes.label: Board status enum
nodes.rationale: Starting, Stopping, Stopped, Throw, Takeout, Takeout in progress, Calibrating, Offline, Setup, Error. status:'Throw' means armed and waiting, not that a dart just landed -- an easy misreading.

nodes.label: Achievements catalogue and progress
nodes.rationale: Progress is written after every dart so bars move during a match rather than only when it ends, and every achievement declares its target statically so a player who has never thrown sees '0 / 10' rather than '0 / 1'.

nodes.label: Four-stage pipeline: Board Manager -> bridge -> server -> frontend
nodes.rationale: Dependencies run one way (schema <- engine <- stats <- server) and nothing imports the bridge; they talk over a websocket, so the vendor-specific stage can be replaced without touching game logic.
nodes.norm_label: four-stage pipeline: board manager -> bridge -> server -> frontend

nodes.label: Unlock celebrations
nodes.rationale: Evaluated after every dart, not at the final whistle, so an unlock is celebrated the moment it happens and persisted immediately -- an interrupted match does not lose it. Multiple unlocks queue rather than stack so a nine-darter shows each in turn; honours prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Electron shell around the unmodified backend
nodes.rationale: The shell starts bridge and server as child processes and points a window at the scoreboard; no game logic lives in it, so the docker deployment and the desktop app run the same program, which is the only way both stay tested. It ships its own Node 24 runtime rather than Electron's embedded Node 20, because the backend needs type stripping and node:sqlite, which Node 20 has neither of.
nodes.norm_label: electron shell around the unmodified backend

nodes.label: Event sources: simulator / autodarts / replay
nodes.rationale: Simulated darts are POSTed to the bridge rather than straight into the game server so they travel the same path a real dart will, keeping the simulated and live paths identical.

nodes.label: @darts/fakeboard stand-in Board Manager
nodes.rationale: simulator and replay bypass the network so neither exercises reconnection, heartbeat or takeout detection; the fake speaks the real local protocol on :3180 so SOURCE=autodarts is testable without hardware. Control endpoints live under /sim, never /api, so nothing there can be mistaken for a real board path. It proves the bridge, not the protocol -- the protocol claim rests on the capture.

nodes.label: Golf handicap (best 8 of last 20 rounds)
nodes.rationale: Playing every hole to personal par scores two points a hole -- 36 over a round -- which is exactly why a new player starts on a handicap of 36. Strokes are spread evenly with the remainder dealt from hole 1 upwards. Each round's verdict is handicap + par target - points, so beating your handicap brings it down and playing to it leaves it alone. It is computed from finished matches like every other statistic, never stored on the profile, and is resolved into the match config at start time so recomputing it later cannot rewrite a round already played.

nodes.label: Dart heatmap
nodes.rationale: Built from segment counts, which scoring always knows, so heatmaps work with coords: null; where coordinates are reported individual darts are plotted on top. Nothing depends on their presence -- the map simply gets sharper when they arrive.

nodes.label: Leaderboard ranking (3 for a win, 1 for turning up)
nodes.rationale: Ranking on win rate alone would put whoever won their only match on top forever; points-first means a season of showing up counts for something and a single lucky night does not. Tie-breaks are win rate, then average, then legs won. Golf handicaps are the one figure that is not seasonal, because a handicap is what the next round is played off.
nodes.norm_label: leaderboard ranking (3 for a win, 1 for turning up)

nodes.label: Match overview / after the game report
nodes.rationale: Opens the moment a game ends and from the Last game button; shows standings, three-dart and first-nine averages, best turn, 180s, checkouts, busts and the full golf card, plus a replay of the winning turn.
nodes.norm_label: match overview / after the game report

nodes.label: Play again / use last game's settings
nodes.rationale: Golf handicaps are deliberately not carried over by either: they move with every round played, and reusing a stale one would misprice the game.
nodes.norm_label: play again / use last game's settings

nodes.label: Local player profiles
nodes.rationale: No accounts and no logins; a rename flows through to historical matches because matches reference the profile rather than copying its name, and deleting soft-deletes so historical matches survive.

nodes.label: Robin Hood achievement
nodes.rationale: Two darts of one turn landing within 5 mm of each other, a shaft's width; within a single turn only, and a turn with any unlocated dart cannot unlock it.

nodes.label: Changing the roster mid-match
nodes.rationale: Join and leave are ordinary log commands, so they replay correctly through undo and survive a restart. A joining player starts on their own full score; removing whoever is throwing ends their turn cleanly.

nodes.label: Round-trip test by angle, not radius
nodes.rationale: The test in adapters/autodarts.test.ts asserts every segment must plot back inside its own wedge by angle, because a radius check could never distinguish the two sign conventions of y.
nodes.norm_label: round-trip test by angle, not radius

nodes.label: @darts/schema as the isolation boundary
nodes.rationale: Our own event, command and view types mean every package downstream of the bridge speaks our vocabulary rather than the vendor's.

nodes.label: Tight Grouping achievement
nodes.rationale: Three darts of one turn inside a 20 mm circle, measured as the smallest circle enclosing all three; compares darts within a single turn only because darts are pulled out between turns, and a turn with any unlocated dart cannot unlock it.

nodes.label: X01 per-player handicaps
nodes.rationale: Per-player overrides of both the start score and the in/out rule, so a stronger player can play 501 double-out against 301 straight-out in the same leg.

nodes.label: This board's camera configuration
nodes.rationale: 3 cameras with indices 0,1,3 but addressed as 0/1/2 in the API; 1280x720 @ 30fps, auto-calibrate on start enabled, motion standby 15 min.

nodes.label: Board geometry (BDO spec radii and number order)
nodes.rationale: Radii in mm normalised by 170: bull inner 7, bull outer 17, treble 97-107, double 160-170, board 225; segment angle 360/20; number order 20,1,18,4,13,6,10,15,2,17,3,19,7,16,8,11,14,9,12,5. Usable directly by our frontend renderer.
nodes.norm_label: board geometry (bdo spec radii and number order)

nodes.label: Event channels and observed rates
nodes.rationale: motion_state is 30/s and very chatty so it must be throttled or dropped in the bridge; cam_stats 3/s, stats 1/s; cam_state and calibration_state were not seen.

nodes.label: Cloud independence of /api/*
nodes.rationale: /api/* is served by the board locally with no Cloudflare headers; only / and /assets/* come from the Autodarts CDN, which is why the stock board UI needs internet and why our own frontend removes that dependency. No api.autodarts.io traffic observed from /api/*.

nodes.label: Coordinate frame: normalised by 170, bull origin, x right y up
nodes.rationale: Same orientation as @darts/schema's Coords, so toCoords only scales and does not flip. Guarded by a round-trip test that asserts every segment lands back inside its own wedge by angle, not by radius.
nodes.norm_label: coordinate frame: normalised by 170, bull origin, x right y up

nodes.label: {type, data} envelope
nodes.rationale: Client dispatches on type and hands data to handlers, so channel routing is a single switch.

nodes.label: Throw/takeout event sequence
nodes.rationale: 'Throw detected' per dart (status Throw while armed, Takeout once 3 are down), then 'Takeout started' while status is 'Takeout in progress' with throws[] still populated, then 'Takeout finished' with numThrows: 0 and no throws key at all -- not throws: [].

nodes.label: segment.bed and segment.name encoding
nodes.rationale: bed is Single/SingleInner/SingleOuter/Double/Triple/Outside; name is a 1-char prefix plus number such as D20 or M20 for the miss ring. The adapter derives the ring from bed and ignores multiplier.

nodes.label: CONFIRMED / FROM BUNDLE / OPEN status legend
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes what was observed on the wire from what was read out of the Board UI's minified JS, where names are reliable but types are not -- so claims carry their own evidence grade.
nodes.norm_label: confirmed / from bundle / open status legend

nodes.label: throws[] is cumulative for the visit
nodes.rationale: The array grew from 1 to 3 entries as each dart landed, each element's segment/coords staying fixed once set -- so the bridge must diff rather than treat each frame as a fresh turn.
nodes.norm_label: throws[] is cumulative for the visit

nodes.label: WebSocket transport ws://<board>:3180/api/events
nodes.rationale: No auth and no subscribe frame -- the server pushes unsolicited on connect. Plain GET returns 400, upgrade returns 101. Stock UI reconnect is a flat 1 s retry.

nodes.label: open-darts (self-hosted darts server)
nodes.rationale: Built on Autodarts camera hardware used purely as a local detection source, with no dependency on api.autodarts.io and no cloud game service, so games keep working without internet and without an account.

nodes.label: The anti-corruption boundary
nodes.rationale: adapters/autodarts.ts is the only file that knows Autodarts field names and boardControl.ts the only one that knows its control paths; everything else depends on @darts/schema. The adapter parses strictly and fails loudly because a silent mis-parse would produce a plausible-but-wrong score and quietly corrupt career statistics; an unexpected payload logs the offending frame and names the file to fix.

nodes.label: The command log is the source of truth
nodes.rationale: Every command is appended to the commands table and match state, career statistics and achievement progress are projections folded from it. Undo and correction edit the log and replay it, which is why undo is correct for every game without each engine unwinding its own state. Three consequences painful to retrofit: new achievements backfill over all history dated to the match that earned them; statistics are fixable retroactively; corrections propagate to match, career stats and achievements consistently.
nodes.norm_label: the command log is the source of truth

nodes.label: coords is nullable and nothing depends on it
nodes.rationale: Game logic, statistics and the scoreboard all work with coords: null because a dart's segment is enough to score it; achievements that need coordinates simply evaluate to nothing for a dart without them. Only visualisations read coords, and they degrade.
nodes.norm_label: coords is nullable and nothing depends on it

nodes.label: No backend build step (Node 24 type stripping)
nodes.rationale: Node 24+ runs the TypeScript sources directly via type stripping and persistence uses node:sqlite built into Node, so there is no compile step and no native module to compile.
nodes.norm_label: no backend build step (node 24 type stripping)

nodes.label: Season as a window on the command log
nodes.rationale: Reset leaderboard deletes nothing: it records a timestamp and the live table counts matches finished after it. The archive keeps only standings and how everyone threw -- heatmaps and golf cards are left out because they are derivable from the command log, which the archive does not replace.
nodes.norm_label: season as a window on the command log

nodes.label: Two board indicators: heartbeat vs running flag
nodes.rationale: The header pill is the bridge's heartbeat -- is the board talking to us -- and the Settings chip is the board's running flag -- is detection actually armed. A board can be perfectly online and detecting nothing, and that is worth seeing. With simulator or replay there is no board, so the buttons grey out and say why rather than offering dead controls.
nodes.norm_label: two board indicators: heartbeat vs running flag

nodes.label: Unlocks are a projection, not a fact
nodes.rationale: Achievements are reconciled after every command in both directions: undo or correct a dart and anything it earned is withdrawn, and a celebration still on screen is pulled. Without this, undo would leave a permanent reward behind and achievements could be farmed by throwing and undoing. There is deliberately no 'stays deleted' flag -- one still earned will be awarded again; to remove it permanently, correct the throw behind it. Achievements from earlier finished matches are never touched by an undo in the current one.
nodes.norm_label: unlocks are a projection, not a fact

nodes.label: Verifying the packed app outside the repo
nodes.rationale: verify-package.mjs runs the packed app from a temporary directory outside the repo because Node resolves bare imports by walking up parent directories, so a packed app sitting inside the workspace would find @darts/* in the repo's own node_modules and pass a test it should fail.
nodes.norm_label: verifying the packed app outside the repo

nodes.label: The y-axis bug that got through
nodes.rationale: The frame was recorded as y down and was wrong: every board-sourced dart plotted mirrored top-to-bottom, a dart at 20 appearing at 3. It survived because each captured dart landed at the radius predicted for its segment, and a radius is identical under either sign of y; the one dart whose angle was examined sat at 9 o'clock where both conventions agree. The lesson: a radius cannot confirm an axis direction.
nodes.norm_label: the y-axis bug that got through

nodes.label: Caveat: the bundle mixes board and cloud clients
nodes.rationale: /tournaments, /stripe, /lobbies, /matches and /users/me are cloud game-service endpoints, not board endpoints -- don't mine the bundle for board paths without checking each against the board first.
nodes.norm_label: caveat: the bundle mixes board and cloud clients

nodes.label: Cf-Ray filtering recon method
nodes.rationale: A real local endpoint returns no Cf-Ray header; unknown paths fall through to the cloud-proxied SPA index.html with a 200, so naive 'is it 200?' probing yields false positives on every path. Filter on Cf-Ray.

nodes.label: A radius cannot confirm an axis direction
nodes.rationale: Any future claim about the board's coordinate frame has to be checked by angle, against a dart that is not on an axis.
nodes.norm_label: a radius cannot confirm an axis direction

nodes.label: state channel is edge-triggered
nodes.rationale: 0 frames in a 45 s idle capture: state fires only on throw or takeout. The bridge must treat it as an event stream, not a heartbeat, and must not infer liveness from it -- use stats at 1/s as the liveness signal instead.

nodes.label: Correction: y points UP, not down
nodes.rationale: Originally recorded as y down (screen convention); both fakeboard and toCoords were built to match, mirroring every board-sourced dart top-to-bottom so a dart at 20 plotted at 3. Missed because the check was predicted radius, which is identical under either sign of y, and the one dart whose angle was quoted (S11 at 9 o'clock, y~0.006) is sign-agnostic. S4 and S1 sit upper-right and were both reported with positive y, which settles it.
nodes.norm_label: correction: y points up, not down

nodes.label: Killer game mode
nodes.rationale: The first dart to land on an unclaimed 1-20 in any ring claims it, and anyone who finds nothing in three darts is handed a random unclaimed number so no one gets stuck. friendlyFire (off by default) makes hitting your own double again after becoming a killer cost you a life, for groups who want the extra risk.

nodes.label: Shanghai game mode
nodes.rationale: Rounds run startRound..endRound (default 1-7); only darts on the round's own number score, at ring value. A single, double and triple of the round's number in one turn is an instant win; otherwise the highest total after the last round wins.

nodes.label: Adding a game: one engine file plus one registry line
nodes.rationale: Keeping game logic pure and registry-driven makes a new mode an additive change.
nodes.norm_label: adding a game: one engine file plus one registry line

nodes.label: Checkout hints and route lighting
nodes.rationale: Hints appear only when the score is actually checkable with the darts left -- on 501, 171 or a bogey number such as 169 the slots stay empty rather than offering advice on a finish that is not there. Under straight-out 20 finishes on S20 rather than D10: same score, far easier dart. The route is recomputed after every throw and respects the player's own out-rule.

nodes.label: Cricket game mode (standard and cut-throat)
nodes.rationale: In cut-throat, points go to opponents who have not closed the number and the lowest score wins.

nodes.label: Ending a game early (END_MATCH / closest to winning)
nodes.rationale: What 'closest' means is the engine's decision -- fewest points left in X01, most in Gotcha, most targets closed in Cricket, most points in Golf -- because only the engine knows its own state shape. Legs and sets already banked outrank progress in the current leg.
nodes.norm_label: ending a game early (end_match / closest to winning)

nodes.label: Golf scored Stableford
nodes.rationale: 18 holes on the board's own numbers (hole 7 is the 7); every dart is a stroke and a hole is holed the moment the number is hit in any ring, so a first-dart hit on a par-4 hole is an albatross. A hole is abandoned one stroke over par, for nothing. Play rotates in ordinary three-dart turns and a half-played hole carries over.

nodes.label: Gotcha game mode
nodes.rationale: Count up to a target, overshoot busts; landing exactly on an opponent's total knocks them back to zero or to previousTurn.

nodes.label: Leg end mode: first checkout vs all-but-one
nodes.rationale: Playing on until all but one player has checked out gives everyone a finishing place while the leg is still won by whoever went out first; with two players the settings are equivalent.
nodes.norm_label: leg end mode: first checkout vs all-but-one

nodes.label: X01 game mode
nodes.rationale: 301/501/701 with straight/double/master in and out, legs and sets, bust handling and checkout hints.

nodes.label: Marks-per-round over completed rounds only
nodes.rationale: Dividing running marks by a fractional round makes the figure meaningless mid-turn -- a treble on the first dart would read as 9.00 MPR.

nodes.label: Desktop auto-update
nodes.rationale: Checks the releases page on startup, downloads in the background and offers to restart; the database lives outside the app so updating and uninstalling never touch it. The installer is not code-signed because a certificate costs real money, so SmartScreen warns on first run.

nodes.label: Tag-triggered draft release
nodes.rationale: Tagging v* builds both platforms and uploads to a draft release so the notes can be written before anyone's app offers them the update.
